summary: Defines a Management Information Base for managing the radio frequency interfaces of systems compliant with DOCSIS 2.0, the cable-modem standard, using SNMP. It covers cable modems and the cable modem termination systems they connect to. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: A cable company needs to check how the cable wire is doing. This is a list of gauges for the radio signals going between a home modem and the company's equipment.

questions: what is the docsis rf mib
how does the docsis offline upstream update work
subtitle: The SNMP MIB that lets operators monitor and configure the radio links of DOCSIS 2.0 cable modems and their head-end.

tldr.problem: Cable operators need a standard way to manage the radio frequency links between cable modems and the cable modem termination system, including the new DOCSIS 2.0 features.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the DOCS-IF-MIB module in SMIv2, organized into base, cable modem and CMTS groups of tables, and says how it fits into the Interfaces MIB.
tldr.outcome: It revises and obsoletes RFC 2670 and is a Proposed Standard; RFC 9141 later updated it.

today: RFC 4546 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 2670 and was later updated by RFC 9141. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: What the MIB Covers
sections.content:
This memo defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing the Radio Frequency (RF) interfaces of systems compliant with the Data Over Cable Service Interface Specifications (DOCSIS). Management happens through the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP), and the module is written in SMIv2 (RFC 2578).

Two kinds of device are managed. A cable modem (CM) is the slave station in a DOCSIS system. A cable modem termination system (CMTS) is the master: it is the only station that transmits downstream and it controls the scheduling of upstream transmissions by its CMs. The specification is derived in part from ITU-T J.122, the DOCSIS 2.0 reference.

The RFC revises and obsoletes RFC 2670, adding DOCSIS 2.0 and Euro-DOCSIS requirements. Existing RFC 2670 objects are kept.
sections.plainLanguage: A cable modem is a student and the head-end equipment is the teacher who decides who speaks and when. This document is the checklist the teacher and students use to report how the line is doing.

sections.title: Structure of the MIB
sections.content:
The module is split into three groups. docsIfBaseObjects covers things that matter to both CM and CMTS, docsIfCmObjects covers the cable modem only, and docsIfCmtsObjects covers the CMTS only.

The base group holds tables for downstream channels, upstream channels, Quality of Service profiles and received signal quality, plus docsIfDocsisBaseCapability, which reports the highest DOCSIS version a device supports. The CM group has MAC, status and service-queue tables. The CMTS group has MAC, status, per-modem status, service, modulation, MAC-to-CM lookup, channel utilization and upstream and downstream channel counter tables.

Rows that the device creates itself usually mix configuration and status objects. Rows meant to be created by the management station are generally restricted to configuration (read-create) objects.
sections.plainLanguage: The gauges are sorted into three drawers: some for both sides, some only for the modem, and some only for the head-end.

sections.title: Textual Conventions and DOCSIS Versions
sections.content:
RFC 2670 defined two textual conventions for power levels, TenthdBmV and TenthdB, both in tenths of a unit (5.1 dBmV is represented as 51). This RFC adds DocsisVersion (docsis10, docsis11, docsis20), DocsisQosVersion (Class of Service for DOCSIS 1.0, Quality of Service for DOCSIS 1.1) and DocsisUpstreamType for upstream burst modulation profile types.

The upstream type values are unknown, tdma, atdma, scdma and tdmaAndAtdma. The CMTS modulation type object lists other, qpsk, qam16, qam8, qam32, qam64 and qam128. A cable modem reports its connectivity state through docsIfCmStatusValue, which runs from other(1) through operational(12), with accessDenied(13) meaning the CMTS sent a Registration Aborted message.
sections.plainLanguage: The document agrees on units and names so every device reports power, version and signal style in the same way.

sections.title: Relationship to the Interfaces MIB
sections.content:
The MIB reuses the Interfaces MIB (RFC 2863). An ifEntry exists for each RF downstream interface, each RF upstream interface, each upstream logical channel and each RF MAC layer. The ifStackTable MUST be implemented so the relationships among these sub-interfaces can be found.

The interface types are docsCableMaclayer(127), docsCableDownstream(128), docsCableUpstream(129) and docsCableUpstreamChannel(205). The RFC's example is a CMTS MAC interface layered over one downstream and two upstream interfaces, each upstream carrying two logical channels.

The RFC then lists, per interface type, how each ifTable column behaves. For example, a downstream interface is output-only at the CMTS, so all ifIn* counters return zero, and input-only at the CM, so all ifOut* counters return zero. The MAC layer interface returns 1500 for ifMtu. Telco Return upstream management is outside the scope.
sections.plainLanguage: Each wire, each lane on the wire and the traffic cop on top gets its own line in a big directory, and the directory says how they stack on each other.

sections.title: Offline Upstream Parameter Changes
sections.content:
Changing the settings of a live upstream channel one SNMP SET at a time could leave it in an inconsistent state. For DOCSIS 2.0 CMTS implementations, the RFC defines a way to prepare changes offline and commit them together. It is supported by CMTSs and not applicable to CMs.

Three objects drive it: docsIfUpChannelStatus (a RowStatus used to create a temporary interface), docsIfUpChannelCloneFrom and docsIfUpChannelUpdate. The steps are:

  • Create a temporary interface by setting the status to createAndWait.
  • Set docsIfUpChannelCloneFrom to the physical interface's ifIndex, which links the two and copies the current parameters.
  • Edit the temporary interface.
  • Set its status to active. This succeeds only if every parameter is valid; otherwise the SET returns commitFailed.
  • Set docsIfUpChannelUpdate to true to transfer the values, then destroy the temporary interface.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of scribbling on the real homework, you copy it, fix the copy, have it checked, and only then swap it in.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC warns that the MIB relates to a system providing metropolitan public internet access, so improper manipulation of its objects may deny service to a large number of end users. The CMTS controls most RF interface parameters, so write access to CMTS objects can compromise users' services. On the CM side, the only read-write object is docsIfCmRangingTimeout.

Setting objects in the downstream channel, upstream channel, modulation and QoS profile tables can negatively alter channel parameters. Setting docsIfCmtsServiceAdminStatus to disabled or destroyed interrupts a modem's service. Some readable tables could also reveal how modems are spread across channels, and the CMTS per-modem table holds MAC and IP addresses that could be used for theft of service.

It is RECOMMENDED to use the SNMPv3 security features, and deploying SNMP versions prior to SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.plainLanguage: If a stranger could flip the head-end's switches, a whole neighborhood could lose internet. So only trusted people should be allowed to read or change these settings.

sections.title: Compatibility With DOCSIS 1.0 and 1.1
sections.content:
RFC 2670 holds the RF interface management requirements for DOCSIS 1.0 and DOCSIS 1.1. The Class of Service (DOCSIS 1.0) requirements are unchanged and live in docsIfQosProfileTable, docsIfCmServiceTable and docsIfCmtsServiceTable. DOCSIS 1.1 and 2.0 Quality of Service management is defined in the DOCSIS OSSI specifications instead.

When a new object has the same function as an old one but greater capacity (for example 64 bits rather than 32), both the original 32-bit object and the new 64-bit object must be implemented.
sections.plainLanguage: New modems and old modems must still understand each other, so old gauges stay and new, bigger gauges are added next to them.

messages.label: SET docsIfUpChannelStatus = createAndWait
messages.note: Creates a temporary interface, which is notReady.

messages.label: SET docsIfUpChannelCloneFrom
messages.note: Associates it with the physical interface and copies its parameters.

messages.label: SET status = active
messages.note: Fails with commitFailed if any value is invalid.

messages.label: SET docsIfUpChannelUpdate = true
messages.note: Transfers the values to the physical interface.
